rules.ind7: Indian-language reads: Wikipedia views in the 12 Indian editions (hi ta te kn ml mr bn gu pa or as bh), 7 UTC days. English is never in this total. '≥' = a floor from the daily most-read lists (top 1,000 per edition; a day off the list counts 0) — no 60-day curve yet.
rules.en_in: English reads FROM India: India's per-country most-read list (all editions), English rows, 7 days. Wikimedia rounds these up, so each listed day is a ceiling. A day off the list is unknown (0 up to that day's list cutoff), so a title listed on only some days shows a range: listed days … + the cutoff of each day off the list. '≤' only when it is on the list all 7 days.
rules.en_world: English Wikipedia worldwide, 7 days — read around the world, so it is KEPT OUT of the Indian total.
rules.change: Indian-language reads vs the 7 days before. Curves only: '—' for a floor.
rules.stage: From the 30-day curve: At peak (last day = 30-day high) · Building (last 3 days ≥ 70% of peak and +15% on the 3 before) · Cooling (below 70% of peak and −15%) · Elevated (holding at 3× its 30-day median) · Steady · Faded. Floor only = no curve. No stage word = a death reported in the last 30 days.
rules.zone: Where the Indian-language reading sits: South = Tamil + Telugu + Kannada + Malayalam editions; Hindi; ≥ 60% = that zone, both ≥ 30% = Both, else '-leaning'. Only with enough reads to split.
rules.agreement: Signals rising: reading (last day ≥ 1.5 × the median of the 7 before; needs a curve) and Google Trending now (on a scan in the last 7 days). 'quiet' = none.
rules.confidence: High = clears an edition floor with articles in ≥ 2 Indian editions, or ≥ 300 Indian reads a day · Med = clears a floor or ≥ 100 a day · Low = otherwise. Floors: Hindi 300 a day; any other edition 20% of that edition's leader this week (≥ 50 in 7 days).
rules.editions: Indian editions with an article on this entity (of 12).
rules.consistent: The newest dated event on file — calendar, Wikidata release / death, Google trending, a main-page feature or the 60-day high. 'Consistent with', never 'because'.
rules.kept: Kept: film, series, web series, song, entertainment person, athlete, sports event or team (Wikidata P31 / P106, or the tracker's registry), with an India link. Politics, places, generic pages and deaths of anyone else are dropped. Held back: writers, poets and spiritual figures (a secondary screen or music occupation is not enough), sport topic pages with no dated event (Cricket, FIFA, Olympic Games) and adult-search traps in any script.
rules.days: Wikimedia days are UTC and publish about a day late.

lens.info_period: views a day 26 Sep–2 Oct 2026 · India share Sep 2026 (Wikimedia top-by-country)

rules.lens: Language lens: rows read in this Wikipedia edition, ranked by its own 7-day reads. Change, stage and the 14-day trend come from this edition's own 60-day curve ('—' / Floor only without one). An edition is its readers, not a state: 'Tamil Wikipedia readers', never 'Tamil Nadu reads'.
rules.share: India's share of the edition's readers (Wikimedia top-by-country, Sep 2026). Under 50% = a weak proxy for Indian readers. '—' = Wikimedia does not publish it for this edition.
rules.hindi: Ten Hindi-belt states read one Hindi edition: Wikipedia cannot split UP from Bihar. Google's state lists can — see the chip.
rules.google: On Google in its home states: the title was on Google's Trending-now list (free RSS, stored hourly sweeps, last 24 h) of a state where the language is spoken. Best rank per state; the time is the newest sweep it was on. Linked by Wikidata id, the tracked universe's trend keys, or an exact name.
